A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same persistent-homology study of adversarial LLM representations. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original analyses of prompt-injection and sandbagging representations, classification results, neuron-level controls, and adaptive-attack experiments in Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds subsampling sensitivity experiments and rank-correlation analyses in Appendix C.2 and Tables 3 and 7.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same global Vietoris–Rips PH pipeline, 41 barcode statistics, correlation pruning, PCA/CCA, logistic regression, and SHAP interpretation, alongside the same neuron-pair local analysis. Added background and parameter tests do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains TaskTracker prompt injections across six models, WMDP-inspired sandbagging on Mistral 7B and LLaMA3 8B, and LLMail-Inject adaptive attacks. Executed/refused/ignored conditions already appear in v2. The new subsampling experiments reuse existing Mistral data.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LDA, linear SVM, and logistic regression on raw activations and SAE features. Its added PH column redisplays the proposed method's previously reported performance; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds tests over subsample sizes 100, 500, 1000, and 1500 and counts 30, 40, 50, and 60, with classification and cluster-distance metrics. Peak analysis adds Spearman correlation. Table 1 changes layer labels from 0/7/14/23/31 to 1/8/16/24/32; the middle row is not explained by simple index renumbering. Main sampling, splits, and controls otherwise remain.

E4.justification: New Figures 15–17 test how subsampling parameters affect classification, within-class concentration, and between-class separation. Rank correlations extend the existing variance-versus-class-separation analysis. Normalization/permutation controls, dispersion resampling, nonconsecutive-layer tests, and adaptive-attack robustness were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 7 newly report Spearman coefficients and significance alongside existing precision-at-k analyses. Permutation testing, five-fold cross-validation, SEM/FDR reporting, bootstrap iterations, and Monte Carlo variance information already appear in v2. No explicit increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises baseline scores, including first-hidden-layer LDA(SAE) accuracy from 0.9875 to 0.995. Figure 15 newly reports first-layer accuracy of 0.57–0.63 with subsample size 100, versus 1.00 at sizes 1000 and 1500. Figures 16–17 add distance results, and Tables 3/7 add correlations and revise some significance markers. Most original PH results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Beyond v2's Rips/barcode introduction and statistic formulas, v3 adds substantial formal background defining Cech and alpha complexes, persistence modules, functorial maps, and interval decomposition, with complexity and containment claims. No new study-specific proof is supplied. The added Cech–Rips containment is inconsistent with the appendix's stated radius definitions.

C1.justification: The central compression, architecture-independence, and neuron-level phase-transition contributions remain. Section 2.2 adds an explicit first-systematic-large-scale-adversarial-PH novelty claim, including 'up to 80B parameters,' although the reported model coverage still ends at 70B. This changes claimed novelty and scope without adding a corresponding experiment.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges that cycles lack semantic interpretation and that analysis is restricted to homology dimensions 0 and 1; computational constraints remain documented in Appendix F. Appendix C.2 adds convergence interpretations for subsampling, and Table 2 makes model/layer exceptions explicit. Much of the expanded dispersion interpretation already existed in v2's appendix.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 documents the new parameter grids and fitting a global StandardScaler to the combined barcode-summary point cloud for cluster-distance analysis. Existing Ripser++ configuration, four 80-GB A100 GPUs, timing/memory measurements, sandbagging data collection, and adaptive-attack preparation remain in relocated appendices.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against prior topology-based neural-network and LLM research, including Naitzat et al., Gardinazzi et al., and Sekuloski et al., and adds geometric-interpretability and formal-PH references. This accompanies an explicit novelty claim and replaces parts of v2's hierarchy-based motivation and cycle-matching discussion. Bibliographic updates to retained works are not counted as new research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion are extensively rewritten; background subsections are reordered, dispersion analysis receives a main-text subsection, and appendices are reorganized from A–C into A–G. Terminology, affiliations, and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different conference layout, adds a cross-model summary table and three ablation figures, and expands comparison and peak-analysis tables. It rearranges and redisplays dispersion panels, presents a shortened local-analysis figure while retaining its full version in the appendix, and relocates nonconsecutive-layer plots. Existing plot data are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new subsampling checks, rank-correlation evidence, clearer limitations, and closer engagement with prior topology research modestly strengthen assessment of the retained findings. These gains are limited by new exposition errors, particularly the inconsistent Cech–Rips containment in Appendix A.1 and confusion between subsample size and count in Appendix C.2. Those errors weaken supporting explanations without establishing a change to the retained computational pipeline.
